title: Embeddings index consistency and rollback workarounds
author: Elena Morales
content:
Overview
--------
This page documents common failure modes we see for customer-managed or Redwood-managed embeddings indexes, recommended short-term workarounds to restore service, and longer-term fixes to prevent recurrence. It is intended for Customer Success, Support Engineers, and the Embeddings SRE/Infra teams.

Scope
-----
- Applies to vector indexes used with Redwood's embeddings API, including: local index servers (faiss/hnsw), managed index service, and third-party vector DB connectors (Milvus, Pinecone, Weaviate).
- Addresses consistency problems (missing vectors, partial queries, index drift), indexing failures during bulk ingest, and rollback/restore guidance.

Impact and priority guidance
---------------------------
- P0: Index returns wrong vectors for >20% of queries, or customer-facing search/generation failures. Immediate page + incident.
- P1: Partial degradation (increased latency, missing results <20%). Open escalation ticket and apply quick fix within 4 business hours.
- P2: Non-critical background failures (reindex jobs failing but fallbacks exist). Track in backlog.

Owners and escalation contacts
----------------------------
- Customer Success (first responder): #cust-success, oncall cs lead (cs-lead@example.com).
- Embeddings Infra / SRE: #infra-embeddings, oncall (infra-emb-oncall@example.com).
- Integrations / Connectors: #platform-connectors.

Detection checklist (signals to watch)
------------------------------------
1) Telemetry / Alerts
- Index error rate > 0.5% for 5m (alert).
- Query hit-rate drop > 30% vs baseline (30d rolling).
- Unexpected reindex job failures with non-zero exit code.

2) Customer-reported symptoms
- Identical queries return different top results across time windows.
- Recently-ingested documents do not appear in search results.
- High latency on embedding-lookup calls.

Symptoms -> Likely causes -> Immediate action (table)
---------------------------------------------------
| Symptom | Likely cause | Immediate action |
|---|---|---|
| Missing recent documents | Partial ingest failure (batch abort) | Re-run incremental ingest for affected batches; verify via sample queries |
| Query returns stale vectors | KV cache serving old embeddings | Invalidate prefix cache for impacted keyspace; force cold read |
| Higher-than-expected false positives | Wrong vector dimension / model mismatch | Validate embedding model version; temporarily route queries to compatible model variant |
| Index returning 500 errors | Index process crash / OOM | Restart index pod; inspect OOM logs; scale up memory if reproduces |
| Inconsistent shard responses | Corrupt shard or split-brain | Quiesce writes, trigger shard re-sync, or restore last known-good snapshot |

Quick fixes (playbook)
----------------------
These are ordered from least intrusive to most. Prefer non-destructive options first.

1) Verification and scoped rollback
- Step 1: Ask customer for a minimal failing query set (3–10 examples) and time window.
- Step 2: Re-run queries against the same index with a strict timestamp filter to reproduce.
- Step 3: If problem is limited to a single ingest batch, re-run the ingest for that batch. Use the ingest job ID and the incremental ingest API: 

  curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.com/v1/ingest/retry" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"ingest_job_id":"INGEST_JOB_ID"}'

- Step 4: Verify results by running the customer's example queries and checking top-5 similarity scores differ from baseline by > 0.

2) Cache invalidation
- When stale vectors are suspected, invalidate prefix/KV cache for the index keyspace: 

  curl -X POST "https://internal-admin.redwood.local/v1/cache/invalidate" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
    -d '{"namespace":"indexes","key_prefix":"index-<INDEX_ID>-kv"}'

- Confirm by comparing timestamps on vectors returned and re-running queries.

3) Snapshot rollback (managed indexes only)
- Preconditions: We have a validated automatic snapshot policy and a snapshot taken prior to the incident.
- Steps: 
  1. Put index into read-only mode (no writes).
  2. Create an incident branch and notify customer of potential write loss after snapshot rollback.
  3. Restore snapshot to a new index instance using the internal restore tool: 

    redwood index restore --snapshot-id SNAPSHOT_ID --target-index restored-index-<INCIDENT_ID> --region us-west-2

  4. Run a smoke test using customer query set. If restored index meets quality checks, perform cutover routing.

- Cutover rollback considerations: keep original index for 72 hours to allow delta reconciliation.

4) Rebuild strategy (when snapshot not available or corrupt)
- Run parallel rebuild to a new index instance. Use staged rollback: 
  - Start incremental rebuild with throttling: redwood index rebuild --source-batch-list BATCH_IDs --throttle 250/s
  - Monitor build success rate and sample top-n results.
  - Once parity reached on verification queries, switch traffic.

Operational validation criteria (minimum before cutover)
-----------------------------------------------------
- Sample accuracy: For customer-provided verification set, top-5 recall >= 95% of baseline or pre-incident run.
- Latency: P95 lookup latency <= 1.5x baseline and absolute P95 < 300ms for managed indexes in production tiers.
- Error rate: < 0.1% 5m rolling.

Permanent mitigations and engineering requests
-------------------------------------------
1) Preflight schema validation in ingest pipeline (reject mismatched dimension vectors).
2) Improve snapshot frequency for high-change customers (default 4h -> 1h for enterprise).
3) Add a lightweight background parity checker that compares recent ingest batches against the index every 30 minutes and alerts on divergence > 5%.
4) Improve connector backpressure behavior to avoid partially applied batches when downstream errors occur.

Monitoring and alerting recommendations for CS/SRE
-------------------------------------------------
- Metrics to surface to customer and internal dashboards: ingest_success_rate, index_build_progress, top_k_recall_on_verification_set, prefix_cache_hit_rate.
- Recommended alert thresholds:
  - ingest_success_rate < 98% for 30m -> P1
  - top_k_recall_on_verification_set < 90% -> P0
  - index_build_progress stalls for > 15m without progress -> P1

Customer communication template (short)
-------------------------------------
Subject: Incident update — embeddings index for <customer-name>

We detected inconsistent search results impacting a subset of queries. We have isolated the affected index and are running an incremental rebuild. Expected recovery window: 2–6 hours. There is no evidence of data exfiltration. We will notify you after verification tests complete or sooner if the window changes.

Next steps we will take:
- Re-run failed ingest batches and validate results
- Restore from snapshot if incremental rebuild fails
- Provide post-incident summary and plan to prevent recurrence

How CS should engage engineering
--------------------------------
1) Open a Priority ticket with embedding-infra and include: customer name, index ID, ingest job IDs, sample failing queries, and timestamps.
2) Ask Infra to create a temporary read-only replica for forensic analysis before any destructive operation.
3) Coordinate customer-facing communications; avoid promising specific cutover times until validation criteria are met.

Post-incident checklist (RCA & follow-up)
----------------------------------------
- Collect: ingest logs, index build logs, snapshot logs, telemetry around cache invalidation, and thread dumps if crashes occurred.
- Determine root cause classification (ingest, cache, index binary, connector).
- Create engineering ticket for permanent fix with owner and target milestone.
- Offer customer a mitigation plan (snapshot frequency change, managed rebuild voucher) depending on severity.

Appendix: Useful CLI snippets and queries
----------------------------------------
- List recent snapshots for index:
  redwood index snapshots --index-id <INDEX_ID> --limit 10 --format json

- Trigger a controlled rebuild for specific batches:
  redwood index rebuild --index-id <INDEX_ID> --batches "batch1,batch2" --concurrency 16

- Sample verification query (embedding + similarity):
  curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings/query" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"index_id":"<INDEX_ID>","query_embedding": [0.123, ...], "top_k": 5 }'

----------

- Index snapshot and restore internal runbook: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/index-snapshot-restore-2025
